summary: Enforce the user-required noalias-disabled Rust CPU oracle and verify compiler attributes before exporting fixtures.
regressions: Reject missing, conflicting or unverified oracle settings in executed and source-only reports
Probe actual optimized LLVM IR for mutable and shared reference attributes
Run original cooperative hub reduction at 0/1/33/63/64/65/129 slots, empty groups, repeated dispatches and 257 hubs in 256 workgroups, in debug and release
Rebuild all registered fixtures under the enforced oracle and rerun C, Metal and Ascend source lowering
differences: Pin only the CPU reference to Rust 1.98.1 because 1.99.1 removed -Zmutable-noalias; use RUSTC_BOOTSTRAP=1 with the exact recorded flag for the oracle and its dependencies. Native Metal stays on 1.99.1.
Enable the pinned khal cooperative CPU runtime to exercise original Rust shared-memory shaders; this does not claim a TileLang hub port yet.
No Rust physics edits or tolerance changes. Disabling a compiler attribute is a required CPU backend workaround, not a claim of language-level aliasing soundness.
Previous evidence without the required configuration is historical and cannot certify current parity. Ascend vendor compilation/execution remain unavailable.
